evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/api_call.rs:106 — reqwest::Client is built (Client::builder().timeout(60s).user_agent(...).build()) without a redirect policy, so it follows up to 10 redirects by default. validate_external_url() (defined line ~151) only vets the INITIAL URL at the call site (~line 250), so a user-configured workflow api_call action pointing at an attacker-controlled host that returns 302 -> http://169.254.169.254/ or an internal service bypasses all SSRF/private-IP checks (cloud-metadata / internal-network exfiltration). Fix: .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none()) or re-validate every hop. Confirmed: grep for 'redirect' in api_call.rs returns nothing.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/api_call.rs:151-159 — validate_external_url parses only the passed-in URL string; there is no per-hop revalidation, so redirect-based SSRF is unguarded. NOTE: same id previously emitted 2026-07-10 & 2026-07-13; still unresolved and not in backlog.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/scheduler.rs:322-324 — self.get_announcement_target_users(announcement).await.unwrap_or_default() collapses any DB/query error into an empty Vec, so on a transient failure the just-published announcement's target-user resolution silently yields [], the `if !target_user_ids.is_empty()` guard skips notification dispatch, and no warn/error is logged and no retry occurs — the published announcement reaches nobody while the scheduler reports success. Should log-and-continue or propagate rather than swallow to []. Fresh (2026-07-15 api-core run flagged a different scheduler issue, mutex-poison).
